A node is PROTECTED when some enclosing ast.Try contains it inside its .body (transitively); a node in a handler / orelse / finalbody is NOT protected by that Try, though an OUTER Try's body still protects it. S2c: manifest_json=NULL (the column IS nullable) -> escaped=true, TypeError('the JSON object must be str, bytes or bytearray, not NoneType'). S11: backfill_text_fingerprints on the same fixture -> escaped=true at 1962. The path is named in NO registered finding: findings.md's F-B10R2-MISSINGFILE supplement lists only the unsupported-handler ingest and _atomic_write; §7sexies does not mention it; r3's B-VR-B10R3-06 registered only those two. r3's own AST check DID list line 1660 and called both remaining parses 'genuine whole-run abort paths (measured in my_probes P6)' - but P6's scenarios were the artifact-metadata column and the missing file, so that attribution was wrong and the path was never registered as a result.
findings.impact: Identical to the P2 this round fixed: one damaged row stops the batch, no ProcessingReport, no per-document failure record, and every queued document behind it is silently unprocessed. It is strictly easier to reach than the fixed one because it needs no parse failure - it fires on the first document whose manifest column cannot be turned into a manifest.
findings.severity_reasoning: P2, not P1, by the same standard r3 applied to the sibling: the column is written only as SourceManifest.canonical_json() and only for observations that become location_status='active' (the scanner's manifest-failure branch writes NULL but also leaves source_id NULL, hence 'quarantined', so normalize's queue cannot select that row). Corruption therefore has to come from outside the product - which is exactly the 'latent robustness hole today' r3 used to justify P2 over P1.
findings.suggested_disposition: Same one-line shape as -01: route the manifest parse through a total helper (e.g. `manifest_state`), or wrap the per-document body in a try that records a failure row. At minimum, register 1660 and 1962 under F-B10R2-MISSINGFILE so the next pass evaluates the whole set instead of a named subset, and extend the probe with the three manifest variants (corrupt / valid-but-incomplete / NULL).

findings.title: The probe's phase-3 evidence is a parser-CONFIGURATION ValueError, not the 'failing document' the commit message and §7sexies describe - the conclusion holds, the label does not
findings.claim: Commit message: 'phase 3 (a deliberately failing document with a malformed artifact row)'; §7sexies: '探针阶段 3（我按它的场景自建）' for a document whose '解析失败'.
findings.evidence: The probe calls normalize_catalog(parser_timeout_seconds=0.001, parser_heartbeat_interval_seconds=0.001); the parser rejects that combination with ValueError('parser heartbeat interval must be less than timeout') BEFORE it touches the document, and the evidence file itself records 'terminal_reasons': {'ValueError': 1}. My S1 reproduces that exact error code and message; my S7/S8/S12 replace the construction with genuine document parse failures (.xls/.pdf without xlrd/fitz, and a real .docx whose document.xml is not a document) and get the same verdict: escaped=false on the reviewed tree, escaped=true at 1727 on the reverted copy. So the fix IS verified - the handler is entered either way - but the evidence as labelled describes a failure the probe never produces.
findings.impact: Low. It matters because 'a failing document' is what a reader will take from the record, and because the round-3 finding was specifically about evidence that does not demonstrate what it is cited for.
findings.suggested_disposition: Say what the scenario is (a parser-argument ValueError entering the failure handler) or add S12's shape (a document whose own bytes cannot be parsed) as the phase-3 fixture.

adjudication_reason: The single live P2 that caused the round-3 REJECT (B-VR-B10R3-01) is genuinely fixed, and I did not take that on the author's word: my own AST map shows the handler's parse is now the total chain and no unguarded parse of the shared column remains; my own minimal repro - a real .docx that cannot be parsed while its existing normalized artifact row carries malformed metadata, with a healthy document queued behind it - gives escaped=false, failed=1, and the healthy document COMPLETED; and the identically constructed copy with that one line reverted escapes with JSONDecodeError at normalizer.py:1727, writes zero normalized.md and leaves the healthy document with no artifact row at all. The author's own probe reproduces the same pair, so the fix is load-bearing rather than incidental. All three round-2 core fixes re-confirm, the registry counts reproduce digit for digit against a scanner I wrote (1 confirmed reader, 12 handoff scopes / 15 sites, 0 readers in the rest of the product package, scripts 2 / tools 0 / tests 10), the gate is 15 cases, the mutation proof re-runs 10/10 killed by assertion with the repository untouched, the unit suite gives exactly the recorded 796, and the four named test files give 35 passed. On the other side: the same defect shape still lives in the same function on the MAIN path (`json.loads(primary["manifest_json"])` at 1660, plus the backfill entry point at 1962), it is measured to abort the whole run and starve healthy documents, and it is registered nowhere - so the class the last two rounds have been closing is still open, with the aggravating detail that this instance needs no parse failure to fire. It is P2 and not P1 because the column is only ever written as canonical JSON for active locations, so corruption must come from outside the product. Four further P3s are text/evidence defects: -05 is not fixed (the new title-bearing .md fixture cannot make the 'consistent' verdict reachable, so phase 2's verdict criterion still isolates nothing, and the new comment claims otherwise), -04 is only partially fixed (findings.md still cites 1725 and now misquotes the evidence file this commit regenerated to say 1739), -03's '已全部改' over-claims while §7ter and §8 still assert the retracted reason and the old generations as current, and the phase-3 evidence is labelled as a failing document when it is a parser-argument ValueError. None of these is a new P0/P1 and no fix introduced a new defect: the attempt_count/terminal arithmetic is unchanged for readable rows (attempt 2 -> 3 -> terminal), a malformed row resets the counter to 1 but the same run rewrites it as valid JSON so it self-repairs and cannot loop, the 'unreadable' state is discarded at the new call site by design and documented in the comment, and the new flag still does not reach the stored artifact metadata. Because the blocking item is cleared and the residue is one live P2 plus evidence/text P3s, the honest verdict is APPROVE_WITH_FINDINGS - the batch may proceed, but the abort-path register is not complete and the record's text is not yet trustworthy on the points listed above.
not_checked: The production catalog was never opened (forbidden), so I cannot say how many real rows carry a damaged locations.manifest_json or artifacts.metadata_json. Every blast-radius statement here is measured on throwaway catalogs.
